message.content: In Christian theology, the figure most central to the faith is Jesus Christ, who is regarded as the Messiah and the Son of God. While Jesus is considered the ultimate fulfillment of prophetic tradition, Christianity also honors many other prophets—such as Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and John the Baptist—who played significant roles in shaping the biblical narrative and theological foundations. Each tradition within Christianity may emphasize different aspects of prophetic history, but Jesus is generally viewed as the pivotal figure around whom Christian belief revolves.
